Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. The clause provides that “[a]ny dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof shall first be referred by the parties to their senior-level executives for attempted resolution through good-faith negotiations.” Compl. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). Should negotiations fail, thirty days after making a written request to initiate those negotiations, “either Party may, by written notice to the other, require that the Dispute be referred to non-binding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association.” Id. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. Skold responds that the language of the mediation clause is permissive (“either Party may ... require”) and also argues that, in any event, Inc. has waived its right to invoke the clause because it participated in litigation over the dispute in the cancellation action before the TTAB. See Pl.’s L.P./Inc. Opp’n at 14-15.
19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). Given the voluntary nature of the latter, this Court agrees with Skold that he was not required to refer this dispute to mediation before bringing suit here against Inc.
20	L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. In essence, they urge this Court to accept the contention that a nonparty to an agreement should be permitted to force a signatory party to engage in negotiations pursuant to a permissive mediation clause in that agreement as a condition precedent to filing suit but cite no relevant case or statute in support of this contention. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
21	Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. 9	"Part I — International ACH and Wire Transactions (NACHA Operating Rules)"  (risk type: 1.3)

12	International ACH and Wire Transactions If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved, and the laws enforced by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”). Under such rules and laws, we may temporarily suspend processing of a transaction for greater scrutiny or verification against the OFAC list of blocked parties, which may result in delayed settlement, posting and/or availability of funds. If we determine there is a violation, or if we cannot satisfactorily resolve a suspected or potential violation, the subject funds will be blocked as required by law. If you believe you have adequate grounds to seek the return of any blocked funds, it is your sole responsibility to pursue the matter with the appropriate governmental authorities. Please see the OFAC website for procedures and form required to seek a release of blocked funds.
13	```

16	
17	```
18	The bulk of Plaintiffs’ breach claim centers around their argument that TD’s conduct violated the NACHA Rules, which Plaintiffs claim were incorporated into the Account Agreement. See Compl. at ¶ 166-67. In order to address this claim we must first determine whether the NACHA rules were in fact incorporated. In support of this point, Plaintiffs cite to page 16 of the Account Agreement, which states in relevant part:
19	International ACH and Wire Transactions

{"clause_id":"c191","reasoning_cat1":"Contains the duplicated words \"agrees to establish establish\", a plain typographical slip that does not change meaning; the risk-allocation for \"anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person\" is stated clearly.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2.2(b)'s funding to the Designated Account and the Designated Account definition (c059).","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.06},

{"clause_id":"c200","reasoning_cat1":"Precise deadlines and confirmation requirements.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Interest Period definition (c092) and 2.12(c).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c201","reasoning_cat1":"A deemed-election rule; the clause uses the singular \"Borrower\" where elsewhere the electing party is \"Administrative Borrower\".","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.12(a) and (b) give the election to Administrative Borrower, while this clause deems \"Borrower\" to have elected; combined with c031's each/either rule, who elects is not perfectly aligned.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.22},

{"clause_id":"c203","reasoning_cat1":"A short, clear disclaimer of matched funding.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the LIBOR Rate definition's reliance on quotation sources rather than actual funding.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c204","reasoning_cat1":"A consideration recital for joint and several liability; conclusory but standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Supports 2.13(b)-(k); the \"mutual benefit\" recital could be tested against the reality that only Fund holds the Notes Receivable, a recital-versus-operative tension.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.23},

{"clause_id":"c212","reasoning_cat1":"Clear enforcement and reinstatement language.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrors 16.7 Revival and Reinstatement of Obligations; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},

{"clause_id":"c215","reasoning_cat1":"A condition precedent expressed with a deeming rule (funding conclusively deemed satisfaction or waiver) and a concrete deliverable.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.4(a)'s filing authorisation and the Filing Authorization Letter definition (c076).","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},

{"clause_id":"c218","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Governing Documents definition (c081) and 5.9.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c219","reasoning_cat1":"\"dated within 36 days of the Closing Date\" is almost certainly an OCR rendering of 30 days, and it differs from the 30-day period in the very next paragraph.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.1(f) (c220) uses 30 days for the same kind of certificate, so the two conditions are internally inconsistent as written.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.20},

{"clause_id":"c221","reasoning_cat1":"Cross-referential and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.8 Insurance supplies the required endorsements; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c222","reasoning_cat1":"\"in form and substance satisfactory to Lender\" with no description of the opinion's content.","reasoning_cat2":"Standard closing condition; no conflicting provision found.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c223","reasoning_cat1":"Specific as to what must be evidenced, with an express Permitted Protest carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Permitted Protest definition (c131) and 6.10.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c224","reasoning_cat1":"A long list of diligence items closed by \"the results of which shall be satisfactory to Lender\" — an entirely subjective condition attached to enumerated specifics.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.1(r), (s) and (u), which use the same formula; nothing contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.06},

{"clause_id":"c227","reasoning_cat1":"Definite documentary condition.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Borrower's Required Procedures definition (c033), which itself requires pre-Closing Lender approval.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},

{"clause_id":"c229","reasoning_cat1":"Names a single specific address; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Relates to the Collateral Access Agreement definition (c049) and 7.15; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c231","reasoning_cat1":"A demanding compliance condition softened by a proviso that it \"may be satisfied by Fund providing to Lender such reasonable assurances as Lender may require\" — the proviso largely undoes the condition.","reasoning_cat2":"Overlaps 5.3, which represents that all aspects of Borrowers' operations and the Offering Circular comply with applicable law; the condition and the representation are not calibrated the same way.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c232","reasoning_cat1":"An enumerated diligence list with a subjective satisfaction standard; conventional for a closing condition.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.1(j) and (s); no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c233","reasoning_cat1":"Specific financial statements identified by period; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 5.11's representation about the latest financial statements delivered before the Closing Date.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c234","reasoning_cat1":"A detailed eight-item delivery list tied to a $250,000,000 threshold; several items are qualified \"if available\", which weakens the requirement in an unspecified way.","reasoning_cat2":"The list differs in content and order from the near-identical list in the Eligible Notes Receivable definition clause (r) (c063), and 3.3(e) and 4.2 repeat the $250,000,000 test; keeping the three aligned is a genuine problem.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c235","reasoning_cat1":"A pure sweep-up condition (\"all other documents and legal matters ... satisfactory to Lender\") appended to a long list of specifics — the classic general-after-specific formulation.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits at the end of 3.1's enumerated conditions and would, read broadly, swallow them; the funding-as-waiver rule in 3.1's opener mitigates this.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c236","reasoning_cat1":"The heading is mis-numbered \"4.2\" in the text although the section is 3.2, and a single condition subsequent (\"a hired a full time Controller\") contains a stray word.","reasoning_cat2":"Making failure of a condition subsequent an automatic Event of Default interacts with Section 8's default list and 3.3's conditions precedent; the numbering slip could confuse cross-references.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c237","reasoning_cat1":"\"true and correct in all material respects\" with an earlier-date carve-out; standard and clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the Section 5 introduction (c262), which uses the same bring-down formula.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c238","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite; the omitted final punctuation is immaterial.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Default and Event of Default definitions and Section 8.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c239","reasoning_cat1":"Specific and objective.","reasoning_cat2":"No conflicting provision found.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c240","reasoning_cat1":"Four words resting entirely on the vague \"Material Adverse Change\" standard, with no time reference for measuring the change.","reasoning_cat2":"The Material Adverse Change definition (c112) supplies content, and 5.11 fixes a baseline date for the representation, but this condition itself specifies no baseline.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c241","reasoning_cat1":"\"otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender\" qualifies an otherwise numeric test; the sentence also ends mid-thought with \"and\".","reasoning_cat2":"Duplicates 3.1(t) and 4.2's $250,000,000 possession requirement; consistent in substance.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c242","reasoning_cat1":"\"a current Borrowing Base Certificate\" — \"current\" is undefined, though 6.2(b) sets delivery timing.","reasoning_cat2":"Read with 6.2(b), which requires a Borrowing Base calculation on the date of each Advance, the requirement is workable.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c243","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed three-year term with an immediate termination right on an Event of Default, qualified by \"subject to any notice and cure rights otherwise provided\"; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Interacts with 3.6 Effect of Termination and 3.7's prepayment premium, which contemplate termination before the Maturity Date; coherent.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c244","reasoning_cat1":"The provision is labelled 3.5 but reads \"3.4 Intentionally Blank\", duplicating the number of the preceding Term section.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.4 is the operative Term provision, so the mis-numbering creates a superficial clash with c243, though nothing turns on a blank section.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c245","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and internally consistent; the cash-collateral parenthetical gives Lender an unqualified determination right but says so expressly.","reasoning_cat2":"Coheres with 3.7 and 2.3(b)(F)-(G)'s cash collateral mechanics; no contradiction found.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c246","reasoning_cat1":"Clear notice period and payment mechanics; the repeated cash-collateral parenthetical is verbose but unambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Works with the Applicable Prepayment Premium definition (c011) and 3.7(b); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c247","reasoning_cat1":"A liquidated-damages style premium payable on any early termination \"for any reason not set forth in Section 3.7(a)\", including foreclosure and plan confirmation, closed by the word \"if applicable\" — which leaves it unclear when the premium is in fact due.","reasoning_cat2":"The premium falls to zero after the first anniversary under c011, so much of the enumerated list is inoperative; the cross-reference in the text is also garbled (\"Section 3.'Mfa)\").","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c248","reasoning_cat1":"A clean grant of security interest; the final sentence flatly bars disposition of \"any item or portion of the Collateral\" except Permitted Dispositions.","reasoning_cat2":"That bar must be reconciled with 4.9(b)'s release-on-sale mechanic, 2.6(a)(iii)'s treatment of sale proceeds and 7.4; whether an unauthorised sale is void or merely a breach is a genuine whole-instrument question.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c249","reasoning_cat1":"Contains an embedded allonge form and a $250,000,000 possession threshold; detailed but with \"otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender\" left open.","reasoning_cat2":"The requirement to hold only $250,000,000 of notes while the Borrowing Base counts all Eligible Notes Receivable leaves a gap between what Lender holds and what it lends against — a real tension with c035 and c063(r)/(s).","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c250","reasoning_cat1":"Remedies are clearly conditioned on an Event of Default, and the trust obligation for Collections is stated plainly.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2.6(a)'s deposit obligation and 4.8's servicing rights; coherent.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c251","reasoning_cat1":"\"any financing statement necessary or desirable\" is broad but is the standard Article 9 authorisation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.1(a), the Filing Authorization Letter (c076) and 4.4(c).","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c252","reasoning_cat1":"Specific three-Business-Day deadline and a defined deliverable.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 5.7(d)'s representation and Borrower Collateral (c032)(c).","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c253","reasoning_cat1":"An open-ended obligation to deliver \"all other documents ... that Lender may request in its Permitted Discretion\", plus detailed IP registration mechanics that sit oddly in a mortgage-fund facility.","reasoning_cat2":"The copyright/patent machinery has little to work on given 5.16 and the nature of the business, and the Real Property mortgage obligation here goes beyond Borrower Collateral (c032), which does not enumerate Real Property.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c254","reasoning_cat1":"Clear assignment of access rights conditioned on an Event of Default.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits 5.5's public-warehouse proviso, which contemplates assigned access; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c255","reasoning_cat1":"An enumerated power of attorney; clauses (a), (c) and (d) are exercisable without any default, which is broader than the rest and could be argued to be inconsistent with the clause's protective purpose.","reasoning_cat2":"The unconditional endorsement power in (d) sits alongside 4.3, which conditions collection on an Event of Default; the difference is deliberate but noticeable.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c256","reasoning_cat1":"Broad inspection rights qualified by \"reasonable notice\" and \"normal business hours\"; clear enough.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.1, 6.2 and 6.5(c)'s appraisal-discussion rights.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c257","reasoning_cat1":"\"any or all reasonable steps\" is loose phrasing, but the Code sections identified give it content.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Control Agreement definition (c053) and 2.6(d); note the liquidation right here is triggered by a mere Default, whereas 4.3 requires an Event of Default.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c258","reasoning_cat1":"Grants Borrowers discretion to take \"such action with respect to the Notes Receivable as the Borrowers may deem advisable\" — a broad subjective standard sitting inside an otherwise controlled servicing regime.","reasoning_cat2":"The revocation right is exercisable \"in accordance with the terms of the Servicing Agreement\", a document not before the reader, and 4.3 gives Lender a parallel right to install a replacement servicer; the two need reconciling.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c259","reasoning_cat1":"Clear trigger (repayment in entirety) and clear obligation; the requirement to return the note \"to facilitate its payment\" after it is already repaid is slightly circular.","reasoning_cat2":"Complements 4.9(b) and (c); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c260","reasoning_cat1":"\"When a Note Receivable is sold by Fund in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, Lender shall release the Lender's Liens\" makes the release turn on the wholly unspecified phrase \"in accordance with the terms of this Agreement\", and \"against payment of the agreed amount therefor\" leaves it unclear who fixes the agreed amount and whether payment is a condition of release.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be squared with Permitted Dispositions (c127)(e), which requires a cash price of at least 80% of the unpaid balance paid directly to a Cash Management Account, with 2.6(a)(iii)'s direct-payment requirement and with 4.1's flat prohibition on disposing of Collateral — whether a sale outside those terms nonetheless releases the Lien is a genuine internal conflict.","prob_cat1":0.56,"prob_cat2":0.62},
{"clause_id":"c261","reasoning_cat1":"Three enumerated triggers with a defined deliverable; \"reasonably acceptable to Lender\" is the only soft element.","reasoning_cat2":"Trigger (ii) uses the same undefined \"in accordance with the terms of this Agreement\" formula as 4.9(b) (c260), so it inherits that provision's uncertainty.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c262","reasoning_cat1":"Standard bring-down language with a materiality qualifier and an earlier-date carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches 3.3(a) (c237); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c263","reasoning_cat1":"\"good and indefeasible title\" is a term of art of contested content, and it is used for personal property while \"good and marketable title\" is used for Real Property.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 7.2 and the Permitted Liens definition; no contradiction found.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c264","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (i) requires the note to be secured by real property \"on which a commercial or residential development is located or is expected to be built\" — \"expected\" by whom, and on what basis, is unstated.","reasoning_cat2":"Clause (i) also conflicts in emphasis with Eligible Notes Receivable clause (a) (c063), which requires a commercial loan for purchasing commercial or residential real estate, and with the Note Receivable definition (c119) requiring maker-owned property.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c265","reasoning_cat1":"\"commensurate with forms and documentation used by prudent lenders in the same or similar circumstances\" is a vague external benchmark, and the flat representation that everything complies with all applicable laws is unqualified by materiality in its second half.","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps Eligible Notes Receivable clause (g) (c063) and 3.1(m)/(p)'s approval of the same forms; the unqualified compliance representation about the Offering Circular is broader than 3.1(q)'s conditional formula.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c266","reasoning_cat1":"\"fit for such purposes\" is a short, soft representation, but the subject matter is trivial in this facility.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Equipment definition (c069) and 6.6.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c267","reasoning_cat1":"The proviso permitting storage of loan files in \"a public warehouse, access to which has been assigned by a Borrower to Lender\" is an exception whose scope (which files, which warehouses) is loosely drawn.","reasoning_cat2":"It cuts against the flat statement in the same sentence that Collateral \"is not stored with a bailee, warehouseman, or similar party\", and 6.9 requires a Collateral Access Agreement for new locations.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c268","reasoning_cat1":"A short, plain representation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.1's accounting system covenant and the Books definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c269","reasoning_cat1":"Schedule-referential; the schedule number is OCR-garbled (\"3.7(a)\") but recoverable.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.9 and the Code's perfection rules; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c270","reasoning_cat1":"Schedule-referential and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.9, which permits amendment of Schedule 5.7(b) on 30 days' notice.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c271","reasoning_cat1":"Schedule-referential and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"No conflicting provision found.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c272","reasoning_cat1":"Definite as of a fixed date.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.4(b)'s obligation for after-acquired commercial tort claims.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c273","reasoning_cat1":"The trailing parenthetical \"(as may be necessary by the applicable laws of such state)\" is garbled and redundant of the preceding clause.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.1(e)-(f) and 6.12; no substantive conflict.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c274","reasoning_cat1":"\"Other than as described on Schedule 5.8 or in an Offering Circular\" makes an unattached, changeable document a carve-out from the representation, leaving its scope indefinite.","reasoning_cat2":"The Offering Circular definition (c122) is itself a collective, amendable bundle, so the carve-out could expand over time against 5.20's fixed Closing Date snapshot.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c275","reasoning_cat1":"Uses corporate share vocabulary for LLC subsidiaries but the meaning is clear enough.","reasoning_cat2":"The Subsidiary definition (c155) excludes several entities, so a \"complete and accurate list\" of Subsidiaries may exclude affiliated funds — coherent but easily misread.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c276","reasoning_cat1":"Same Offering Circular carve-out as 5.8(b), applied to Subsidiaries.","reasoning_cat2":"Same interaction with c122 and the narrowed Subsidiary definition; consistent in structure with 5.8(b).","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c277","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line authorisation representation; standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.1(c)'s resolutions certificate.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c278","reasoning_cat1":"\"material contractual obligation\" is undefined, but the clause is otherwise a conventional no-conflict representation.","reasoning_cat2":"Clause (iii)'s carve-out for Permitted Liens aligns with 7.2 and 5.9(e).","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c279","reasoning_cat1":"Clear and bounded.","reasoning_cat2":"Sits against 3.1(q), which contemplates that licences and approvals may be required for the Investor Membership Interest offering; the two are not obviously aligned.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c280","reasoning_cat1":"Standard enforceability representation with the usual bankruptcy/equity exceptions.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 16.4 Severability; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c281","reasoning_cat1":"States the Liens are \"validly created, perfected, and first priority\" as of the representation date, which is a legal conclusion rather than a fact but is standard.","reasoning_cat2":"\"subject only to Permitted Liens\" is in tension with the assertion of first priority, since Permitted Liens (c130) includes categories that would rank ahead; 2.1(b)(ii) expressly contemplates superior-priority Liens.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c282","reasoning_cat1":"A triple-nested set of exclusions (\"other than ... and other than ... and other than\") makes the sentence hard to parse, and \"reasonably could not be expected to result in a Material Adverse Change\" inverts the usual formulation.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent in substance with 6.3(g)'s litigation notice requirement, which uses the more usual \"reasonably could be expected\" phrasing.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c283","reasoning_cat1":"Clear baseline (\"since the date of the latest financial statements submitted to Lender on or before the Closing Date\") and standard GAAP carve-outs.","reasoning_cat2":"Supplies the baseline that 3.3(d) (c240) lacks; the two provisions therefore need to be read together.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c284","reasoning_cat1":"A four-word representation resting entirely on the defined term \"Solvent\".","reasoning_cat2":"The Solvent definition (c150) uses only a balance-sheet test, which does not match the fraudulent-transfer concepts invoked by the heading of Section 5.12 and by 5.12(b).","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c285","reasoning_cat1":"Tracks the statutory actual-intent language; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Sits with 5.12(a) and the Solvent definition; the section addresses intent but not constructive fraudulent transfer, a gap rather than a conflict.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c286","reasoning_cat1":"A flat negative representation; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Benefit Plan and ERISA Affiliate definitions; no covenant elsewhere contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c287","reasoning_cat1":"Knowledge-qualified in (a) and (b) but not in (c) and (d), an asymmetry that could matter.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.13's environmental covenants and the Environmental Lien definition.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c288","reasoning_cat1":"An absolute representation extending to fees payable \"by Borrowers or any other Person\", which no Borrower could reliably know.","reasoning_cat2":"No indemnity or covenant elsewhere addresses broker fees, so the representation stands alone.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c289","reasoning_cat1":"Standard IP representation with a schedule; the singular \"its business\" against plural Borrowers is a minor slip.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.4(c)'s IP registration covenants, though those covenants are more elaborate than this business requires.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c290","reasoning_cat1":"\"peaceful and undisturbed possession\" and \"material to their business\" are soft but conventional lease representations.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.11's covenant to pay rent and the Permitted Protest carve-out.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c291","reasoning_cat1":"A schedule-based listing requirement; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.7 Control Agreements and 2.6; \"as updated from time to time\" is unaccompanied by any update mechanic, unlike 6.9.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c292","reasoning_cat1":"\"taken as a whole\" appears three times and materially changes what the representation covers; a court would have to decide what unit of information is being tested.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits with 6.14 Disclosure Updates, which requires correction of untrue statements but expressly says notification does not cure the earlier breach; the two are consistent.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c293","reasoning_cat1":"\"such detail ... as is satisfactory to Lender\" makes the adequacy of the schedule a matter of Lender's judgment inside a representation of truth and completeness.","reasoning_cat2":"Schedule 5.20 is also the list of permitted Indebtedness under 7.1(b), so its content has covenant consequences; consistent in structure.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c294","reasoning_cat1":"Straightforward schedule representation with an anti-affiliate condition.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Approved Title Insurance Company definition (c013), which allows Lender to add or remove companies, and with the Affiliate definition (c008)'s special 10% rule.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.12}
]}

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c295","reasoning_cat1":"A standard covenant chapeau; \"so long as any credit hereunder shall be available and until payment in full of the Obligations\" is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"The Section 7 chapeau (c319) adds \"until termination of this Agreement\" whereas this one does not, a small asymmetry between the affirmative and negative covenant periods.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c296","reasoning_cat1":"\"information as from time to time reasonably may be requested by Lender\" is open-ended but the core obligation is definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.2's reporting requirements and 5.6's records representation.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c297","reasoning_cat1":"The reporting table is badly mangled in the executed text, with the timing column interleaved into the item descriptions, so which frequency attaches to which report is genuinely hard to read; item (h) is also an unbounded \"such other reports ... as Lender may request\".","reasoning_cat2":"The daily/monthly deadlines here must be squared with 3.3(f)'s requirement of a \"current\" Borrowing Base Certificate at each Advance and with 6.3's monthly financial reporting; the mangled table makes that harder.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c298","reasoning_cat1":"Contains several mechanical slips — \"with 30 days after the end of each month\" for \"within\", and a cross-reference rendered \"Sections 7.16 and 217\" — inside an otherwise detailed reporting covenant; clause (h) is an unbounded catch-all.","reasoning_cat2":"It calls Sections 7.16 and 7.17 the \"applicable financial covenants\" although 7.17 is a collateral-quality limit, and it requires an unqualified audit opinion measured against those same covenants; also relevant is 7.16(b)'s defective ratio.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c299","reasoning_cat1":"A placeholder with no content.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 8.2 lists the covenants whose breach is an Event of Default and omits 6.4 while including 6.15, which is also \"Intentionally Omitted\"; the inconsistency is cosmetic.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c300","reasoning_cat1":"The heading is mis-numbered \"6.3\" although the section is 6.5, and clause (a) stacks \"commercially reasonable efforts ... to the extent that it is commercially reasonable to do so and in a commercially reasonable manner\", a circular triple use of the same standard.","reasoning_cat2":"The duty to collect is expressly \"Subject to Section 4.8\", which allocates servicing to Borrowers or Servicer; and 9.1(e)/(o) let Lender take over — the three fit together but only with care.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c301","reasoning_cat1":"\"necessary or useful in the proper conduct of its business\" and \"material leases\" are soft, but this is standard maintenance covenant language.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 5.17 Leases and 6.11.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c302","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and definite, with express Permitted Protest carve-outs; \"proof satisfactory to Lender\" is the only soft element.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.1(i), the Permitted Protest definition and Section 10's self-help right.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c303","reasoning_cat1":"\"all other hazards and risks as ordinarily are insured against by other Persons engaged in the same or similar businesses\" is a general catch-all after specific perils, and \"as sole loss payee ... or additional insured, as appropriate\" leaves the choice unstated.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.1(g) and 6.8(b)-(c); Section 10(c) gives Lender force-placement rights if this covenant is breached.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c304","reasoning_cat1":"Clear $50,000 threshold and disbursement mechanics; \"staged payment terms reasonably satisfactory to Lender\" is the only soft term.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.8(a) and 2.3(b)'s application rules; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c305","reasoning_cat1":"\"concurrent in form or contributing in the event of loss\" is technical insurance language, but its meaning is settled.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.8(a); no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c306","reasoning_cat1":"A clear location covenant with a 30-day notice amendment mechanic, though \"Schedule 5.7\" is cited without the subsection letter.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires a Collateral Access Agreement for any new location, which sits against 5.5's and 7.15's public-warehouse proviso permitting storage where access has merely been assigned.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c307","reasoning_cat1":"Compliance is qualified by the Material Adverse Change standard, importing that vague term.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits against 5.3, which represents compliance with all applicable laws without any materiality qualifier — the covenant is markedly softer than the representation.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c308","reasoning_cat1":"Short, definite, with a Permitted Protest carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 5.17 and the Permitted Protest definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c309","reasoning_cat1":"Introduces separateness covenants using \"all reasonable steps, including ... all steps that Lender may from time to time reasonably request\" — an open-ended obligation and a corporate-formalities requirement applied to LLCs.","reasoning_cat2":"The separateness regime sits awkwardly with 2.13's joint and several liability and with 7.13's permitted affiliate transactions and management/servicing arrangements with Bar-K.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c310","reasoning_cat1":"\"observe all corporate formalities as a distinct entity\" is vague as applied to a California LLC, which has no corporate formalities as such.","reasoning_cat2":"The Governing Documents definition (c081) contemplates LLC operating agreements, so the corporate vocabulary is a mismatch with the actual entities.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c311","reasoning_cat1":"Clear separateness requirement for books and assets.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 6.1 and the Books definition; note that 6.12(b) is missing from the sampled sequence, which suggests a gap in the executed document.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c312","reasoning_cat1":"The double exception (\"except as herein specifically otherwise provided\" and \"except for the Cash Management Accounts or as required by any written agreement between Fund and an Account Debtor\") makes the scope of the no-commingling prohibition hard to fix; the closing words appear to prohibit maintaining any bank account at all.","reasoning_cat2":"Read literally it would bar the Designated Account required by 2.8 and the Escrow Accounts required by 2.6(e) and 6.17, so it cannot be applied without harmonising against those provisions.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c313","reasoning_cat1":"Four enumerated environmental covenants, each with a defined trigger; \"reportable quantity\" is externally defined.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 5.14 and the Environmental Lien/Remedial Action definitions.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c314","reasoning_cat1":"Clear notification duty with an explicit statement that notification does not cure or amend.","reasoning_cat2":"Sits deliberately against 5.19 Complete Disclosure and the various \"as updated from time to time\" schedules, which it prevents from being self-amending.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c315","reasoning_cat1":"A placeholder with no content.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 8.2(a) nonetheless makes failure to observe Section 6.15 an Event of Default, an internal oddity since there is nothing to observe.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c316","reasoning_cat1":"\"To the extent necessary to comply with Section 4.2\" imports that section's $250,000,000 threshold, but the covenant then speaks of delivering \"all original promissory notes\", which is broader — the two halves point different ways.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.2 requires delivery of only enough notes to reach $250,000,000 absent a default, while Eligible Notes Receivable clause (r) and 3.1(t) impose delivery requirements on every note; the three are hard to reconcile.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c317","reasoning_cat1":"Clear deposit obligation with an inclusive list of escrow categories.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires deposit into \"a Deposit Account that is subject to a perfected Lender's Lien\", whereas 2.6(e) requires Escrow Accounts at Cash Management Banks under Cash Management Agreements; the two describe the same duty differently.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c318","reasoning_cat1":"The covenant requires escrow instructions calling for the documents \"listed in Section 3.3(z)\", but Section 3.3 has only clauses (a) through (f) — the cross-reference has no referent.","reasoning_cat2":"The intended reference is presumably 3.1(t), whose document list is the one used elsewhere (4.2, 8.17); as written the covenant cannot be applied without repairing it against those provisions.","prob_cat1":0.44,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c319","reasoning_cat1":"Standard negative-covenant chapeau; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It runs \"until termination of this Agreement and payment in full\", while the affirmative covenant chapeau (c295) omits the termination limb; a minor asymmetry.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c320","reasoning_cat1":"The lettering runs (a) through (f) and then jumps to \"(z) endorsement of instruments or other payment items for deposit\", a plain mechanical error in the enumeration.","reasoning_cat2":"Clause (b) permits Indebtedness \"set forth on Schedule 5.20\", tying the covenant to a schedule described in 5.20 as a Closing Date snapshot; Approved Debt and Subordinated Debt in (d)-(e) then interact with 7.7 and 7.10.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c321","reasoning_cat1":"A short prohibition keyed to the defined Permitted Liens, with a well-drawn replacement-Lien parenthetical.","reasoning_cat2":"Its operation depends entirely on the Permitted Liens definition (c130), whose clause (c) proviso about Approved Debt Liens is grammatically broken.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c322","reasoning_cat1":"Broad prohibition (including any amendment of Governing Documents) with a single exception for a Permitted Reorganization.","reasoning_cat2":"The exception depends on the Permitted Reorganization definition (c133), which is anchored to an extrinsic written description; whether a given restructuring qualifies is the crux.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c323","reasoning_cat1":"\"except incidental to a Permitted Reorganization\" appears twice in one sentence, making the drafting clumsy but the meaning clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Same dependence on c133 as 7.3(a); consistent in structure.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c324","reasoning_cat1":"\"all or any substantial part of its assets\" is an undefined quantum, and the clause sits directly against 7.4, which prohibits disposing of \"any\" assets.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.4 (c325) prohibits any disposition other than Permitted Dispositions, so 7.3(c)'s narrower \"substantial part\" test is redundant at best and inconsistent at worst.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c325","reasoning_cat1":"An absolute prohibition on disposing of \"any\" assets subject only to Permitted Dispositions; short and stark.","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps 7.3(c) and 4.1's last sentence, and its practical content is set entirely by the Permitted Dispositions definition (c127) and the release mechanic in 4.9(b).","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c326","reasoning_cat1":"The prohibition covers names, EINs, organizational numbers and state of organization, but the proviso permits only name changes on notice — the mismatch leaves the other changes absolutely barred, perhaps unintentionally.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.9's amendment mechanic covers locations and chief executive offices but not organizational identity; 5.7 fixes those details on schedules with no update mechanic.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c327","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence begins with three carve-outs before reaching the prohibition, and \"the curtailment in the origination of new loans\" is an unbounded exception that could permit the business to be wound down entirely.","reasoning_cat2":"That exception sits uneasily with 7.14's use-of-proceeds contemplation of making new Eligible Notes Receivable and with the Triggering Event definition's $500,000,000 portfolio floor.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c328","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (c) prohibits amendments \"in any manner that would be adverse to any Borrower\" — an odd formulation, since a covenant for Lender's benefit would normally bar amendments adverse to Lender.","reasoning_cat2":"The opening carve-out for payments permitted by 7.10 and refinancings under 7.1(f) ties this covenant to those provisions; the Approved Debt payment permission is the operative escape.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c329","reasoning_cat1":"One line resting on the defined term; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Depends on Change of Control (c044), which keys to Permitted Holders (c128) and to Subsidiaries in existence at the Closing Date; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c330","reasoning_cat1":"\"advance notice to, and consent by, the Lender\" specifies no notice period and no standard for consent, and \"in any material respect\" is undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"The Borrower's Required Procedures definition (c033) already requires prior written Lender approval in Lender's sole discretion for any amendment, so this covenant duplicates and slightly contradicts that standard.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c331","reasoning_cat1":"The exception permitting distributions \"to the extent required or permitted by Fund's Governing Documents\" is an unbounded carve-out that lets an amendable extrinsic document define what the covenant allows.","reasoning_cat2":"Read against the Restricted Payments definition (c142), 7.7 and the Permitted Reorganization machinery, this exception could permit the very member redemptions the covenant appears designed to control; the cross-reference is also mis-rendered as \"Section 6.30b)\".","prob_cat1":0.42,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c332","reasoning_cat1":"A single long sentence combining a fiscal-year/accounting-method restriction with an accountant-access condition; awkward but comprehensible.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 1.2, 6.3's accountant-consultation rights and the GAAP definition.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c333","reasoning_cat1":"Short prohibition with two exceptions keyed to defined terms.","reasoning_cat2":"Depends on Permitted Investments (c129) and Permitted Reorganization (c133); the reorganization exception is unqualified and broad.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c334","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (c) forbids \"any other transaction\" with an Affiliate except those that are \"in the ordinary course\", \"upon fair and reasonable terms\", \"fully disclosed to Lender\" and \"no less favorable ... than would be obtained in an arm's length transaction\" — a general catch-all after two specific prohibitions, resting on four undefined evaluative standards; the opening sentence about forming Subsidiaries also sits oddly under the section heading.","reasoning_cat2":"Its exceptions run to Permitted Dispositions (c127), Permitted Investments (c129), Section 7.10 payments and Permitted Reorganizations (c133), and \"Affiliate\" carries a special 10% deeming rule under c008 expressly \"for purposes of ... Section 7.13\"; whether transfers to affiliated entities were permitted turns on how all of these fit together.","prob_cat1":0.54,"prob_cat2":0.55},
{"clause_id":"c335","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (b)(ii) permits proceeds to be used for \"working capital and general corporate needs ... including funding of its obligations with respect to any Investor Membership Interests or pursuant to a Permitted Reorganization\" — an elastic permission whose outer edge is undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"That permission has to be read against 7.10's Restricted Payments prohibition and the Approved Debt/Subordinated Note machinery, since funding member withdrawals with Advance proceeds is both contemplated here and constrained there.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c336","reasoning_cat1":"A prohibition immediately undercut by a proviso permitting public-warehouse storage of certain loan files; \"loan files that do not include original promissory notes, Lien instruments, or assignments\" is a workable but fine distinction.","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates almost verbatim the proviso in 5.5 (c267) and interacts with 6.9's Collateral Access Agreement requirement; the three are close but not identical.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.24},

{"clause_id":"c347","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed $200,000 threshold; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Permitted Liens (j) excludes judgment Liens that are \"not an Event of Default hereunder\", so the two provisions define each other circularly.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c348","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (z) — \"any other agreement ... the termination of which is reasonably likely to result in a Material Adverse Change\" — is a general catch-all after two specifics, and the qualifier attaches to termination rather than to default.","reasoning_cat2":"Clause (x)'s reference to \"capital obligations to any member or former member in connection with their Investor Membership Interests\" interacts directly with 7.10 and the Approved Debt/Subordinated Note machinery, where such obligations are expressly contemplated.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c349","reasoning_cat1":"Clear trigger with an exception keyed to the subordination provisions.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 7.7(b) and 7.10(b), which permit payments to the extent the Subordination Agreement allows.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c350","reasoning_cat1":"\"any material misstatement or misrepresentation\" in any \"warranty, representation, statement, or Record\" made by any employee or agent is very broad, with no knowledge or notice qualifier.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5's representations are already qualified \"in all material respects\", so this clause layers a second materiality test; 6.14 requires correction but says correction does not cure.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c351","reasoning_cat1":"Clear trigger; the Validity Agreement itself is not attached, so what \"terminated by operation of law\" means depends on that document.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Validity Agreement and Validity Agreement Party definitions (c162, c163) and 3.1(b)(iii).","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.10},

{"clause_id":"c357","reasoning_cat1":"A clear acceleration remedy with an express subjection to the Code's commercial-reasonableness requirements.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.1(o)'s automatic acceleration on insolvency defaults and with 3.4's termination right; coherent.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c358","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.3's conditions precedent and 8.5's interim relief from the obligation to extend credit.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c359","reasoning_cat1":"Clear termination remedy preserving Liens and Obligations.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.4, 3.6 and 3.7(b), which contemplate Lender-elected termination and the prepayment premium.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c360","reasoning_cat1":"\"for amounts and upon terms which Lender considers advisable\" is a purely subjective standard, though limited to the post-default period.","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates the power of attorney in 4.5(f), which applies the \"Permitted Discretion\" standard instead — the two provisions describe the same power differently.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c361","reasoning_cat1":"The clause ends by providing that amounts incurred \"shall be Lender Group Expenses\", a term that appears nowhere in the definitions — the defined term is \"Lender Expenses\".","reasoning_cat2":"Because Lender Expenses are charged to the Loan Account under 2.5(c) and paid first in the 2.3(b) waterfall, the undefined \"Lender Group Expenses\" cannot be slotted into that machinery without repair; 9.1(o) repeats the same error.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c362","reasoning_cat1":"\"such payments and do such acts as Lender considers necessary or reasonable\" is broad, and the license to occupy premises \"without charge\" is stated without time limit.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 10's self-help rights and 4.4(d)'s storage-access assignment; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c363","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed setoff right with an express waiver of advance notice and a post-hoc notification duty; carefully drafted.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.1(h) and with the Cash Management Agreement provisions in 2.6(b), which limit the banks' own setoff rights.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c364","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Overlaps 9.1(g) and 3.6's cash collateral mechanic for Bank Product Obligations; cumulative rather than conflicting.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c365","reasoning_cat1":"The list of physical remedies (ship, reclaim, finish, repair, prepare for sale, advertise) and the IP license are drawn for a goods-based borrower and fit awkwardly with a mortgage fund's collateral.","reasoning_cat2":"Borrower Collateral (c032) does include Inventory and Equipment nominally, and 5.16 shows there is essentially no intellectual property, so the clause has little to operate on.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c366","reasoning_cat1":"\"as Lender determines is commercially reasonable\" places the Code's objective standard in Lender's own judgment, a familiar point of friction.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 9.1's chapeau already subjects all remedies to the Code's commercial-reasonableness requirement, which qualifies this self-judging language.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c367","reasoning_cat1":"Specific 15-day notice period with exceptions tracking the Code; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 12, whose deemed-receipt rules expressly carve out Code enforcement notices.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c368","reasoning_cat1":"Labelled \"(h)\" in the text although it falls at position (l), a lettering error; the substance is one short sentence.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.1(j)'s sale right; the mis-lettering runs through the rest of Section 9.1.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c369","reasoning_cat1":"Clear, with an express \"to the maximum extent permitted by law\" qualifier on the no-notice receivership.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.2's cumulative remedies; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c370","reasoning_cat1":"Labelled \"(m)\", duplicating the preceding clause's letter, and consists of a pure catch-all (\"all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity\").","reasoning_cat2":"The catch-all sits after a detailed enumeration and alongside 9.2's cumulative-remedies clause; duplicative but not contradictory.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c371","reasoning_cat1":"Again refers to amounts becoming \"Lender Group Expenses\", an undefined term, and \"deems necessary\" appears twice as a self-judging standard.","reasoning_cat2":"The automatic acceleration on 8.4/8.5 insolvency events contrasts with 9.1(a)'s elective acceleration, and the servicing takeover duplicates 4.3(b) and 9.1(e); the cross-reference to \"Section 8.5\" is garbled.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c372","reasoning_cat1":"Standard non-waiver and cumulative-remedies language; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 15.2, which says the same thing in different words — duplication rather than conflict.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c373","reasoning_cat1":"\"in its sole discretion and without prior notice\" governs a list ending in reserves \"as Lender deems necessary\", an unbounded self-help power.","reasoning_cat2":"It permits reserves against the Borrowing Base at any time, whereas 2.1(b) says Lender \"agrees not to establish any such reserves unless a Triggering Event has occurred and is continuing\" — a direct tension between the two provisions.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.41},
{"clause_id":"c374","reasoning_cat1":"A compact waiver list; the trailing words \"on which such Borrower may in any way be liable\" are ambiguous as to what they modify.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the broader waivers in 2.13(e); no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c375","reasoning_cat1":"Carefully conditioned on Lender complying with its Code obligations, then exculpates broadly; the structure is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 9.1's commercial-reasonableness chapeau and 11.3's indemnity carve-out for gross negligence.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c376","reasoning_cat1":"A long indemnity ending with an all-caps clause extending it to the Indemnified Person's own negligence, then a carve-out for gross negligence or wilful misconduct; the tension between those two sentences is the classic indemnity dispute.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 11.2, 16.11's separate indemnity and the Lender Expenses definition; the survival sentence matches 14.1(b)'s preservation of Section 11.3 rights.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c377","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed notice mechanics; the deemed-receipt rule (\"the earlier of the date of actual receipt or three (3) Business Days after the deposit thereof in the mail\") is workable but the sentence is convoluted.","reasoning_cat2":"The Lender address given here (Dallas, Texas 75244) differs from the address printed on Exhibits B-1, C-1 and L-1 (75254), an internal inconsistency in the same instrument.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c378","reasoning_cat1":"An unqualified New York choice-of-law clause; standard and clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits against 2.13(g)-(h), which waive specific California Code of Civil Procedure defenses, and the Code definition's mandatory-law proviso; those provisions assume California law may govern aspects of the deal.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c379","reasoning_cat1":"Exclusive New York venue with a one-sided option for Lender to sue elsewhere; drafted plainly but distinctly asymmetric.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 13(a); the asymmetry is deliberate rather than inconsistent.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c380","reasoning_cat1":"A standard, clearly expressed jury waiver with a knowing-and-voluntary recital.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 13(a) and (b); no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c381","reasoning_cat1":"The final sentence dispenses with the Eligible Transferee requirement for assignments accompanying a disposition of \"all or any substantial portion of the business or loan portfolio\" — an undefined quantum that can swallow the restriction.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits against the Eligible Transferee definition (c064) and 14.2, and the reference to \"the assigning Lender\" imports plural-lender drafting into a single-lender facility.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c382","reasoning_cat1":"Refers to \"the rights and obligations of a Lender\" and \"an assigning Lender\" in a facility with one Lender, and asserts that an assignment \"shall effect a novation\", a legally loaded characterisation.","reasoning_cat2":"The preservation of Section 11.3 and 16.8 obligations is consistent with those sections; the plural-lender vocabulary is a carry-over from a syndicated form.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c383","reasoning_cat1":"A deemed-amendment provision limited \"to the extent, but only to the extent, necessary\"; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It operates without Borrower signature, which sits against 15.1's requirement that any amendment be signed by Lender and Administrative Borrower.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c384","reasoning_cat1":"A long but tightly enumerated participation regime with specific carve-outs (A)-(E); the drafting is precise.","reasoning_cat2":"Participants are made Indemnified Persons under 11.3 while being denied direct rights here, a deliberate combination; consistent with the Participant definition.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c385","reasoning_cat1":"Short, with an express subjection to the confidentiality section.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 16.8(f), which requires prospective assignees to agree to confidentiality.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c386","reasoning_cat1":"Clause (ii) — a pledge to \"any Person providing financing or other credit support to Lender or any of its Affiliates\" — is far broader than the Federal Reserve carve-out that precedes it, and both override every other provision.","reasoning_cat2":"It expressly trumps 14.1(a)'s Eligible Transferee restriction and 14.2's assignment controls, so the enforcement of such a pledge could bypass the assignment regime entirely.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c387","reasoning_cat1":"Clear, with \"absolutely void ab initio\" for prohibited Borrower assignments.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 14.1; the phrase \"except as expressly required pursuant to Section 14.1\" acknowledges the notice conditions there.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c388","reasoning_cat1":"Clear writing-and-signature requirement with a specific-instance limitation; the carve-out for Bank Product Agreements is express.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires Administrative Borrower's signature for any amendment, whereas 14.1(c) deems the Agreement amended on assignment without any signature — a genuine inconsistency.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c389","reasoning_cat1":"Standard non-waiver language; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Duplicates 9.2's second half almost exactly; redundancy rather than conflict.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c390","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence, definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 3.1 makes the initial extension of credit subject to conditions precedent, but effectiveness of the Agreement itself is separate; coherent.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c391","reasoning_cat1":"The second sentence — \"Unless the contrary is compelled by the context, everything contained in each Section applies equally to this entire Agreement\" — is an unusual and opaque instruction whose effect on the many section-specific provisions is hard to state.","reasoning_cat2":"Read literally it would generalise section-limited rules such as the Affiliate 10% deeming rule (c008) and 1.2's financial-covenant meaning of \"Borrower\", which are expressly confined to particular sections.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c392","reasoning_cat1":"An express disclaimer of contra proferentem coupled with a recital that \"this Agreement has been reviewed by all parties\"; whether such a clause can displace the rule is itself contestable.","reasoning_cat2":"It bears directly on how every one-sided provision in the instrument (Lender's sole discretion, Permitted Discretion, satisfaction standards) would be construed, so it is the natural battleground for a Category 1.3 argument.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c393","reasoning_cat1":"The clause says only that provisions are \"severable ... for the purpose of determining the legal enforceability of any specific provision\" — it never states what happens if a provision is held unenforceable, which is the whole point of a severability clause.","reasoning_cat2":"That gap matters against 2.5(e)'s usury savings clause and 2.13(d)'s \"irrespective of the validity ... of this Agreement\", which assume some machinery for partial invalidity.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c394","reasoning_cat1":"Long but carefully constructed gross-up with a defined \"Taxes\", a net-income exclusion and a gross-negligence proviso; the internal reference to \"the penultimate sentence of this Section 16.5\" is imprecise.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the \"Taxes\" cross-reference in the definitions (c159); the \"without setoff, counterclaim, or other defense\" opener aligns with 2.3(a).","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c395","reasoning_cat1":"Standard counterparts clause with an express statement that failure to deliver originals does not affect validity.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 1.4's rule that a Record satisfies writing requirements; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c396","reasoning_cat1":"\"or elects to do so upon the reasonable advice of its counsel\" lets Lender revive Borrower liability by voluntary election, a notably one-sided trigger.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2.13(i)'s reinstatement provision; the Voidable Transfer definition (c164) cross-refers here correctly.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c397","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list of seven exceptions, each specific; clause (d)'s \"as requested or required by any Governmental Authority\" is broader than the rest but still bounded.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 14.1(e) and the survival reference in 14.1(b); the two-year survival is a clear term.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c398","reasoning_cat1":"A pure statutory notice with no operative obligation on either party.","reasoning_cat2":"Free-standing; nothing elsewhere depends on it.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c399","reasoning_cat1":"The clause bars contradiction by \"any other agreement, oral or written, before the date hereof\" — it says nothing about contemporaneous agreements and contains no conventional merger language, leaving its exclusionary reach uncertain.","reasoning_cat2":"The instrument repeatedly incorporates extrinsic material (Borrower's Required Procedures, the written description underlying a Permitted Reorganization, the Offering Circular), which sits uncomfortably with an entire-agreement clause.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c400","reasoning_cat1":"Combines an irrevocable agency appointment (which the same sentence then makes revocable on notice) with a broad indemnity against claims by \"any third party whosoever\"; the irrevocable/revocable pairing is internally awkward.","reasoning_cat2":"The indemnity's carve-out refers to \"any Lender\" and \"Lender-Related Person\" inconsistently with the operative words, and the appointment interacts with 2.13's joint and several liability and the \"Borrower\"/\"Borrowers\" definition (c031).","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c401","reasoning_cat1":"A form with blanks left unfilled and bracketed alternative text still in place, so the notice cannot be read as a completed instrument.","reasoning_cat2":"The Lender address shown (Dallas, Texas 75254) differs from the notice address in Section 12 (75244), and the recital omits \"between\" and mis-describes the parties compared with the preamble.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c402","reasoning_cat1":"Paragraph 6 certifies compliance with \"Sections 7.16, and 7.37\" — there is no Section 7.37, and the stray comma compounds the error; paragraphs 2 and 5 also duplicate each other with different carve-outs.","reasoning_cat2":"The intended reference is 7.17, which 6.3 identifies as the financial covenant to be certified, so the exhibit is out of step with the operative reporting provision.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c403","reasoning_cat1":"A form with unfilled blanks and bracketed optional text; otherwise clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2.12(b)'s LIBOR Deadline and the Interest Period definition, but the address again reads 75254 rather than Section 12's 75244.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c404","reasoning_cat1":"Names an account holder as \"B-4 PARTNER, LLC\" rather than B-4 Partners LLC, and the schedule combines a specific account with an open-ended substitution formula.","reasoning_cat2":"The Designated Account definition (c059) simply points to this schedule, but the schedule adds a Control Agreement requirement not stated in 2.8; and 2.6(a) requires Wells Fargo to be the sole Cash Management Bank after 60 days while this account is at Greater Bay Bank.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c405","reasoning_cat1":"The account number is redacted or garbled in the executed text, but the substitution formula is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2.3(a) and 2.6(b)(iii), which direct payments and sweeps to Lender's Account.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c406","reasoning_cat1":"Item 2 refers to \"the Subordinated Liens securing Approved Debt\", a capitalised term that is not defined anywhere in the Agreement.","reasoning_cat2":"It presupposes that Approved Debt will be secured, which cannot be squared with Subordinated Debt (c152)(a)'s \"unsecured\" requirement, and it depends on the grammatically broken proviso in Permitted Liens (c130)(c).","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c407","reasoning_cat1":"A short factual list of two licences; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.3 represents that this schedule lists \"all\" required licences for the business as conducted and \"proposed to be conducted\", which is a strong claim against so short a list.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c408","reasoning_cat1":"Two entries, one of which is a location described only functionally (\"at Lender's offices or office of a custodian\").","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.5 represents Collateral is located only at scheduled locations while permitting public-warehouse storage of certain loan files; this schedule does not list any warehouse.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c409","reasoning_cat1":"Short and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"\"SUBSIDIARIES - NONE\" is consistent with Schedule 5.8 and with the narrowed Subsidiary definition (c155), even though covenants throughout address Subsidiaries at length.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c410","reasoning_cat1":"A single address; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches the 3.1(o) landlord waiver location and Schedule 5.5.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c411","reasoning_cat1":"The organizational identification numbers are illegible or redacted in the executed text, so the schedule as reproduced states nothing usable.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.7(c) represents that these numbers \"are identified on Schedule 5.7(c)\", so the illegible entry undercuts that representation and 7.5's prohibition on changing them.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c412","reasoning_cat1":"One word; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 5.7(d) and 4.4(b)'s after-acquired claim mechanic.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c413","reasoning_cat1":"Long and narrative, with a stray comma in \"5,871,017,93 Units\" and a description of Units and Interests that does not map cleanly onto the defined terms \"Stock\" and \"Investor Membership Interest\".","reasoning_cat2":"It discloses that members' Interests are redeemed in the Manager's discretion in the ordinary course, which is squarely in tension with 7.10's prohibition on Restricted Payments (including redemptions) and with the Permitted Reorganization machinery.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c414","reasoning_cat1":"A short narrative disclosure with a typographical slip (\"who's mortgage\"); its content is factual rather than operative.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.10 carves out matters disclosed here from the no-litigation representation, and the second paragraph describes a senior lien on property securing a loan — relevant to Eligible Notes Receivable clause (b)'s first-priority requirement.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c415","reasoning_cat1":"One word; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"It confirms that the elaborate IP covenants in 4.4(c) and the IP license in 9.1(i) have nothing to operate on — surplusage rather than conflict.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c416","reasoning_cat1":"Account numbers are partly redacted and the entries are compressed, but the accounts are identifiable by function.","reasoning_cat2":"It lists Greater Bay Bank as holding the Cash Management Account, which 2.6(a) requires to move to Wells Fargo within 60 days, and Schedule 2.6 (Cash Management Banks) is not reproduced at all.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c417","reasoning_cat1":"Two short items; definite, though item 1 simply cross-refers to Schedule 5.8 rather than giving the detail 5.20 requires.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.1(b) permits only Indebtedness \"set forth on Schedule 5.20\", so the single Fremont Bank loan is the entire permitted stock of existing debt — a tight fit with Permitted Liens item 1 on Schedule P-1.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c418","reasoning_cat1":"The list is reproduced as a mangled two-column table in which company names run together (\"Land America Title Insurance Company -Ticor Title Insurance Company Co.\"), so which entities are approved cannot be read with confidence.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 5.21 and the Approved Title Insurance Company definition (c013) make this list operative for eligibility and Settlement Agent purposes, so the garbled entries matter to those provisions.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.22}
]}
